text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: eu-west-1 continuous-batching streampack path p99 spike. p95=380ms, p99=2.6s over 5m window. Streaming stalls increased ~3.8x. Paging on-call.

sara: oncall ack. tagging infra + ml. Which packer shard? any tenant skew?

ops-bot: tags -> path=continuous_batching_streampack, shard=shard-7, pool=pack-stream-7, model=redwood-gpt-13b-q4, traffic_type=streaming.

raj: I just pulled scheduling metrics. Queue depth for pack-stream-7 jumped and fairness counters show a tenant (convo-proxy) occupying 60% of active slots with several requests >3k tokens. Mixed seqlen pattern.

mike: traces show long KV reads and sync paging on a subset of hosts. A few request traces show packing waited ~45ms for a large request to finish, then everything shipped and tails popped.

vivian: customer ops: we have 2 customers reporting degraded interactive latency (AcmePay, Pixellink). No 5xxs yet but some client-side reconnects on streams.

emily-cs: flagged AcmePay to AMs, they're monitoring. They asked if we're actively mitigating.

sara: mitigation discussion: conservative short-term: 1) lower pack wait window on this shard (reduce packing latency), 2) enable packer-level hetero-shed to avoid waiting for giant reqs, 3) route heavy seq reqs to dedicated pool if available. Long-term: revisit packer preemption fairness.

raj: on point 2 -> we have a `hetero_backoff_enabled` flag but it's off on pack-stream-7 (left off after last perf run). Suggest flip on and set `hetero_threshold_tokens=2048`.

mike: flips I'd do: `max_batch_wait_ms: 12 -> 4`, `hetero_backoff_enabled: false -> true`, `hetero_threshold_tokens: 2048`, and temporarily mark pack_shed_mode=probabilistic at 0.8 for oversized packs. That will reduce throughput but should cut p99 tails.

infra-bot: running patch: `PATCH /runtime/pools/pack-stream-7` payload: `{"max_batch_wait_ms":4,"hetero_backoff_enabled":true,"hetero_threshold_tokens":2048,"pack_shed_mode":"probabilistic","pack_shed_prob":0.8}`. Applying to hosts h-301,h-302,h-303.

deploy-bot: config rollout in progress. No restart required. Changes committed to runtime config and will be picked up by packer processes.

mike: also bump KV soft eviction target from 70% -> 60% to reduce synchronous eviction pauses. I'll apply to the host-level runtime.

jon: quick check: do we have any long-running rolling updates or heavy compiles on these hosts? Could be interference.

raj: no planned compiles in eu-west. I've verified those hosts have steady CPU. The pattern is clearly packing delays.

sara: ok after config applied, let's watch p95/p99 and stall rate. If not improved in 10m, we'll enable routing rule to divert long-seqlen requests to dedicated-dyn pool in eu-west-1 (if capacity) or fallback to hosted smaller model variant.

ops-bot: config patch completed on h-301,h-302,h-303 at +20s.

mike: seeing early telemetry: p95 down to 220ms, p99 trending -> 900ms (from 2.6s). Streaming stalls down 60%. Good sign.

vivian: AcmePay: said latency feels better but wants to know cause. I've told them we're mitigating and will follow up.

raj: followup note: heatmap shows remaining p99 spikes correlate with requests that include large context window + heavy sampling (top-p 0.95). Might be we should throttle sampling on interactive streams for oversized contexts.

sara: don't change model defaults mid-incident unless needed. Add a routing rule instead to opt-out heavy sampling for oversized contexts or route them.

mike: I've drafted a temporary route: if request.tokens_estimate > 2500 then route to `dedicated-oversize-eu` or apply `max_generation_tokens=512` clamp. Need approval.

jon: approve routing clamp to 512 for oversize contexts as emergency mitigation. We should alert product owners.

emily-cs: confirmed with AcmePay that temporary clamp is acceptable; they prefer stability. I'll notify AM.

sara: implement clamp and keep monitor for 30m. If stable, we'll roll back shed/prob settings? Decision: keep hetero_backoff enabled for 24h, revert pack_shed_prob after 2h to avoid long-term throughput loss.

infra-bot: applying routing rule: `POST /runtime/routing` payload: `{"match":{"tokens_estimate_gt":2500},"action":{"route":"dedicated-oversize-eu","gen_token_clamp":512}}` -> applied.

ops-bot: new routing rule applied at +4m.

mike: after routing clamp, p99 settled to ~420ms, p95=210ms, stall rate baseline. We'll keep an eye.

vivian: AcmePay confirmed connectivity restored and interactive experience improved. Pixellink still seeing some flakiness, investigating if they hit same oversize patterns.

raj: next steps: 1) postmortem with packing telemetry + protocol to enable hetero_backoff in more pools, 2) add metric alert for pack wait > 20ms with tenant skew, 3) consider packer preemption to avoid head-of-line waits.

sara: handing off to night oncall in 30m if stable. If regress, page immediately. I'll prepare a short incident slack summary for ops-incident channel and a customer impact note for CS.

emily-cs: thanks — I'll draft the CS note and include the temporary clamp and timeframe.

ops-bot: incident status -> mitigated (initial config + routing clamp). Paging cleared.

sara: handing off to jon (night). Jon, monitor eu-west-1 pack-stream-7 for 2h and ping if p99 > 800ms or stall rate > baseline*2.

jon: ack. I'll take it. Leaving updates in this thread.

ops-bot: log: incident_id=INC-2026-1959998888, severity=sev2, start=1959998888, mitigated=1959999188, actions=[patch_pack_config,enable_hetero_backoff,apply_routing_clamp], affected_customers=[AcmePay,Pixellink].

sara: adding follow-up owners: raj (root cause + packer fairness), mike (KV paging tuning), vivian/emily-cs (customer comms). Closing thread once postmortem doc link is posted.

vivian: will schedule postmortem sync.

ops-bot: incident thread closed for active paging."
